newsitem.title: USA: Hot IPOs due this week as market swings back.
newsitem.headline: Hot IPOs due this week as market swings back.

text.p: Several hot initial public offerings are due this week as Wall Street's appetite for new issues has returned, whetted by several strong deals over the past week and more favorable conditions for stocks.
The following IPOs are expected to generate strong premiums this week:
-- Abercrombie & Fitch Co is "the best stock on the board this week," according to IPO Financial Network president David Menlow. The causalwear retailer gets high marks from other analysts as well.

The company, a unit of Limited Inc, posted 1995 net income of $14.3 million on sales of $235.7 million, according to a regulatory filing. The Limited will control about 95 percent of Abercrombie's voting power after the IPO.
Abercrombie & Fitch had 100 stores in operation at the end of 1995, plans 29 more in 1996, and aims to grow that number by 20 percent annually for the next several years.

Goldman Sachs is the lead underwriter of the offering of seven million shares, to price in an estimated range of $14 to $16 each. The company will use proceeds of the offering to pay down debt and plans no dividends.
The brandname, established in 1892, outfitted the safaris of Teddy Roosevelt, Ernest Hemingway and the expeditions of Admiral Byrd to the North and South poles.

-- American Residental Services Inc will use proceeds from its IPO to acquire acquire seven "founding" companies, making it the leading U.S. provider of comprehensive heating, ventiliating and air conditionaing systems (HVAC) systems.
The Houston-based company would have posted 1995 income from continuing operation of $3.5 million on revenues of $114.6, according to a regulatory filing.
The company provides services in Houston, Washington, Baltimore, Richmond, South Carolina, and central Indiana.

-- Cox Radio Inc's offering also looks hot, analysts say. After completing an acquisition, it will become one of the 10 largest U.S. radio broadcasting companies with 42 stations in cluster areas including Los Angeles, Atlanta, Miami, Tampa and Orlando.
On a proforma basis, it would have posted net revenues of $178.6 million and broadcast cash flow of $51.8 million for the 12 month period ended June 30, 1996.

Cox Radio will use $107.1 million of the $120 million of proceeds to pay down debt to parent company Cox Enterprises Inc, which will own 72 percent of the equity and control 96 percent of the voting power of Cox Radio after the IPO.
Cox Radio opened its flagship Atlanta AM station in 1939 and its first FM statio in Atlanta in 1948.

-- Intelligroup Inc, an information technology services company based in Iselin, N.J., will offer 2.5 million shares in an estimated price range of $8 to $10. Vince Slavin, who tracks IPOs for Cantor Fitzgerald, gives the stock a strong rating.

-- Nitinol Medical Technologies Inc develops medical products using nitinol, a nickel-titantium alloy that has special elastic memory characteristics so products can be transformed into their proper shape once inside the body.

The products are designed to make make medical procedures less invasive, reducing patient trauma, shortening procedure and recovery times, and lowering treatment costs. The company will offer three million shares in a range of $9 to $12.
-- Printer software company Peerless Systems Inc, based in El Segundo, Calif., should have a strong market debut, analysts say.
-- Israeli company Orckit Communications Ltd appears headed for a strong debut despite its warnings that it expects to incur losses at least through 1997.

The company designs systems that allow telephone companies to provide high speed transmsision of data over copper telephone wires. Demand for its services has surged as a result of the explosive growth of the use of the Internet.
"It could rise a point to a point and a half at its opening, and that's on the conservative side. This is an area the market should be coming after in a big way," said Menlow.
